matches.rationale: Both identify that the abstract fabricates a sample complexity of d^{O(1/ε)} (or exp(O(log d/ε))) which contradicts the actual bound of d^{O(1/ε^2)} in the theorems.

Both flag that the abstract overstates the lower bound as exp(Ω(1/ε)) and implies tightness, whereas the actual Theorem 4.3 only yields exp(Ω(ε^{-1/6})), and the upper bound has a different polynomial gap.
No finding mentions the fabricated citation [ZKL23] or the unsupported claim about prior work lacking sub-exponential dependence on d.
No finding discusses the reversal of arguments in the Bregman divergence definition.
No finding addresses the claim that TreeCal requires no knowledge of ρ when parameter settings explicitly depend on ρ.
No finding discusses the contradiction between TreeCal being nearly identical to Pen25 and the framing of TreeSwap-based novelty.
No finding addresses the misleading 'independent of d' claim for the ℓ2 ball bound.
No finding mentions a corrupted strong convexity inequality direction.
No finding mentions the overstatement that the work 'completely solves the high-dimensional calibration problem'.

Both identify an inconsistency in the constant used in the swap regret bound: the ground truth notes the constant 3 was changed to 1 in Theorem C.1, and the finding observes a factor discrepancy between the theorem and its proof.
No finding mentions missing funding or conflict-of-interest disclosure.
No finding discusses the inconsistency regarding BTL being unimplementable yet its regret being used in the analysis.
No finding discusses the misattribution of TreeSwap novelty despite citing prior work.
Both identify that Claim C.3 has the inequality direction reversed (≥ instead of ≤), contradicting the proof and the rest of the analysis.
No finding mentions the hidden requirement of central symmetry for the convex set, which the ground truth flags as an overstatement of generality.
No finding discusses the omission of computational cost analysis for maintaining and sampling from distributions at tree nodes.
Both identify that the calibration error definition inserts a spurious 1/T factor, making it an average error while subsequent results treat it as a total error.
Both identify that the exponent in Theorem 4.3 is d^{1/7} instead of the correct d^{1/14}, altering the lower bound.
